field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The fishing remained the same here in Santa Cruz . There were rock fish, lingcod, and halibut caught up the coast near 4 Mile and Davenport. The deep water anglers caught a mix of rock fish and bonito. The anglers near Capitola caught a mix of halibut and rock fish. There are still a few sea bass being caught near Capitola and Aptos. The water conditions have been calm with light winds and small swells.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast September 3, 2026 Cool Water, Rain Spark Klamath Salmon Push Eureka resident Michael Marcelli with a nice king salmon taken earlier this week on the lower Klamath. Water conditions, as well as fishing, should be good through the holiday weekend. Photo courtesy of Alan’s Guide Service Following some excellent salmon fishing in the Klamath estuary over the past few weeks, adult fall-run king salmon are now beginning to make their way upriver. There are a couple of reasons for the push. First, cool water releases from behind Lewiston Dam began last Friday to help reduce the risk of disease in the salmon. The other factor is the weather. Cooler outside temperatures, along with a fair amount of rain, can do wonders for river temperatures. Combined, these conditions should produce a steady stream of kings moving upriver and staging in the various holes throughout the lower river. But don’t give up on the estuary just yet—the fishing was reportedly pretty wide-open on Monday. I think it’s safe to say we’re smackdab in the middle of what could be a pretty good run of kings. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: All boats have been tied to the docks the past two days due to an early fall storm which hit the area Tuesday night. As of 2pm on Thursday the ocean is coming down and all of the boats are scheduled to be back on the water in the morning.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: SNB did not run as the crew was fishing the ITC tournament on other boats. Pretty much everyone did well today, 30-40 fish, and big ones. It looks like the anchovies finally got big enough and the tuna are back on top. The fish are finally inside the 125 line. Time to make up for some spotty early fishing. ​Mike C Skunked. Ouch. Thank god the wind is going to turn over the water.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) in consultation with the Pacific Fishery Management Council (PFMC), the States of Oregon and Washington, and fishery representatives met today via conference call and have taken the following in-season management action related to the recreational ocean salmon fishery in the area from Leadbetter Point, Washington to Cape Falcon, Oregon: ACTIONS TAKEN: • Effective 12:01 AM Friday, September 4, 2026, the ocean recreational fishery in the area between Cape Falcon and Leadbetter Point (Columbia River Subarea) is open to fishing for salmon. Two salmon per day. All coho must be marked with a healed adipose fin clip. Chinook may not be retained. Possession of Chinook onboard a vessel is prohibited. Columbia River Control Zone is closed.
